instructions.question: Which single intent best describes `newest_inbound` in the context of `thread`?
instructions.focus: Classify the newest inbound message. A specific question or explicit priority condition outranks general interest.

interested.means: Accepts the offer or wants to hear more without asking a more specific question.

question_product.means: Asks what the product does, how it works, or what the process is.

question_cost.means: Asks about price, budget, contract length, or commercial terms.
question_cost.not_when: Do not choose interested when any cost question is present.

question_us.means: Asks who we are, how we found them, or why we contacted them.

not_now.means: Interested in principle but names or implies a later time horizon.
not_now.not_when: A named later horizon remains not_now even when the wording is warm or accepts the offer.

not_relevant.means: Says this is outside their role, company, or remit and gives no colleague to contact.
not_relevant.not_when: If a colleague or role to contact is provided, choose referral.

already_using.means: Already uses a supplier, tool, internal process, or in-house solution.
already_using.not_when: Having an existing solution is already_using, not hard_no, unless they separately demand no further contact.

referral.means: Points to a colleague, named role, or other contact who may be relevant.
referral.not_when: A referral outranks the decline or wrong-person wording wrapped around it.

hard_no.means: Explicitly refuses or asks not to be contacted again.

acknowledgement.means: A pure closing courtesy with nothing to answer.
acknowledgement.not_when: Any new question or request, including one introduced after thanks, is not an acknowledgement.

out_of_office.means: An automatic absence or out-of-office response.
out_of_office.not_when: Choose out_of_office even if the automatic text also sounds interested or includes contact details.

unclear.means: The message does not provide enough evidence to choose any other intent.
